chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic:
'Are those who know and those who do not know alike? Indeed, only those possessed of understanding take heed.'
He said: 'We are those who know, and our enemies are those who do not know, and our Shias are the ones possessed of understanding.'

key_terms.أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ: Those possessed of understanding — the Shias who recognize and follow the Imams
key_terms.الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ: Those who know — the Imams as bearers of divine knowledge
key_terms.عَدُوُّنَا: Our enemies — those who oppose the Imams and are spiritually ignorant

ai.seo_question: Who are 'those who know' and 'those possessed of understanding' in Quran 39:9 according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) provides an authoritative esoteric interpretation of Quran 39:9. He identifies the Imams of the Ahlulbayt as 'those who know' — the divinely-guided bearers of true religious knowledge — while their enemies are 'those who do not know.' The Shias, by virtue of their adherence to and recognition of the Imams, are identified as 'those possessed of understanding' (ulu al-albab). This teaching contextualizes Quranic epithets within the Shia understanding of the special role of the Imams as vessels of divine knowledge.
